concept: Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures
summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas RAG retrieval versus generated-answer evaluation fixtures. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Atlas’s overall fixture contains question, ground_truth and generated answer, omitting contexts. Its answer_similarity output compares answer meaning with the reference; answer_correctness additionally measures factual agreement with that reference. (medium confidence)

RAGAS v0.1.21 defines answer_correctness as a weighted combination of semantic similarity and factual overlap. Its factual component classifies statements into shared facts, answer-only facts and omitted reference facts, then computes an F1 score. (medium confidence)

The inspected Atlas fixture maps question to QUESTIONS and correct_answer to GROUND_TRUTH. Its source context supplies corpus text; evaluator contexts instead contains retrieved doc.page_content lists. The retrieval Dataset contains question, ground_truth and contexts, without a generated answer. Its ground_truth is a reference-answer string, rather than a list of relevant document identifiers. (low confidence)

Atlas inspects per-question output through result.to_pandas() and answer_correctness < 0.7. It warns that wrong references and sentence-versus-short-answer differences can depress scores. (low confidence)

Atlas’s completion-model fixture adds generated answer to question, ground_truth and retrieved contexts, but selects faithfulness and answer_relevancy. Google’s implementation corroborates that these two named metrics do not require ground-truth answers. (medium confidence)

Atlas’s completion loop generates an answer through the chain, then separately invokes the retriever to populate evaluation contexts. Consequently, the code does not capture the exact generation-time retrieval result as its evaluation artifact. (low confidence)

Atlas passes that three-field fixture to context_precision. Ragas v0.1.21 judges each retrieved chunk against the question and reference answer, then rewards relevant chunks appearing earlier in the returned order. (medium confidence)

Atlas context_recall uses the same reference-answer fixture. Ragas v0.1.21 defines its score as the fraction of ground-truth statements attributable to retrieved context, so this output measures reference-statement coverage. (medium confidence)

Fixture names require explicit mapping: Atlas stores generated text as answer and its reference as ground_truth; the independent Hugging Face cookbook stores generated_answer and true_answer, then judges against the latter using a 1–5 rubric. (medium confidence)
